La société y apparaît de plus en plus en colère, avec un retour du clivage gauche-droite très net.

Mais dans l’ancien protectorat, la langue de Sihanouk recule face à l’anglais et au chinois. Elle ne survit plus que dans quelques filières universitaires, et dans le vocabulaire du quotidien.

lemonde.title: « L’organisme, en état d’alerte, se prépare à s’opposer » : ce que la colère produit dans le corps
lemonde.description: « Nos émotions : la colère ». Réponse de notre système nerveux face à une menace, une injustice, une frustration, la colère est une émotion complexe, car profondément subjective. Variant de la simple irritation à la fureur. Des études montrent que, mal régulée, elle augmente les risques d’infarctus et d’AVC, et peut même « briser le cœur ».

lemonde.title: Au Yémen, le camp gouvernemental redéploie des renforts autour d’Aden, menacée par les houthistes
lemonde.description: Le redéploiement des troupes gouvernementales de la région de Bab Al-Mandab vers la capitale provisoire va permettre aux houthistes de consolider leur contrôle du détroit stratégique de Bab Al-Mandab, qui relie l’Asie à l’Europe via le canal de Suez.

lemonde.title: « On reçoit des coups de fil avec des menaces de saisir un avocat » : quand les parents contestent les décisions scolaires dans les grandes écoles
lemonde.description: La propension grandissante des familles à demander des justifications sur les notes et les dossiers de leurs enfants, déjà observée au lycée, apparaît désormais dans le supérieur. Dans les écoles de commerce en particulier, les frais engagés, de plus en plus lourds, les poussent à exiger un retour sur investissement.

france24fr.title: Ariane Chemin: "ce bannissement, c'est mélanger une influenceuse propagandiste, et des journalistes"
france24fr.description: Parallèlement à sa guerre en Ukraine et ses attaques hybrides à l'encontre de nombreux pays européens, la Russie mène une guerre informationnelle. C'est dans ce contexte que s'inscrivent les dernières restrictions imposées par Moscou aux  journalistes étrangers. Les derniers à en avoir fait les frais sont les journalistes français Ariane Chemin et Paul Gogo, qui aux côtés de deux députés, Sacha Houlié et Arthur Delaporte, ont été déclarés personae non gratae par le Kremlin.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle au Cap-Vert : début du dépouillement après une journée électorale calme
france24fr.description: Les bureaux de vote sont désormais clos dimanche au Cap-Vert et les opérations de dépouillement des résultats du premier tour de l'élection présidentielle ont débuté. Cet archipel d'Afrique de l'Ouest connaît une croissance dynamique mais peine à endiguer l'exode de sa jeunesse.

france24fr.title: Fabio d'Andrea : "les COP sont très importantes, l'accord de Paris à l'époque a été un pas énorme "
france24fr.description: La COP 31 Se déroule depuis lundi à Antalya en Turquie. La co-présidence turque et australienne met l'accent cette année sur l'électrification comme levier d'action, avec pour objectif affiché de porter la part de l'électricité dans la consommation finale mondiale d'énergie à 35% en 2035 contre environ 23% aujourd'hui. Le climatologue Fabio d'andrea, chercheur au CNRS, spécialiste de la physique du climat, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Yémen : les Houthis à 60 km d'Aden, le gouvernement place des renforts autour de la ville
france24fr.description: Après une avancée dans le gouvernorat de Lahj dans le sud du Yémen, les Houthis ne se trouvent plus qu'à 60 km environ de la ville d'Aden, siège du gouvernement yéménite. L'armée yéménite a annoncé déployer des combattants supplémentaires autour de la capitale provisoire Aden.

france24fr.title: Au Pérou, Léon XIV dénonce "l'abandon" par l'État des communautés autochtones
france24fr.description: Un mois après son opération pour un cancer du poumon, Léon XIV se rend dimanche à Cusco, dans les hautes Andes péruviennes, pour une étape particulièrement exigeante de sa tournée en Amérique du Sud. Lors d'un discours, le souverain pontife a dénoncé "l'abandon" par l'État des communautés autochtones du Pérou et la privation de leurs droits fondamentaux.

france24fr.title: Éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : qui peut se qualifier, qui est en danger ? Le point sur la 4e journée
france24fr.description: La quatrième journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 se disputera les 16 et 17 novembre et pourrait déjà sceller les premières qualifications pour la compétition. Découvrez groupe par groupe les enjeux de cette nouvelle journée de confrontations sur le continent africain.

france24fr.title: En Israël, la formation d'un gouvernement piétine
france24fr.description: Les tractations s'intensifient en Israël pour tenter de former un nouveau gouvernement. Les équipes de négociation du Likoud et de Yashar se réunissent pour discuter des conditions d'un éventuel accord et des contours d'une future coalition. Explications d'Antoine Mariotti, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: MMA : Ciryl Gane conserve sa ceinture de champion des poids lourds de l'UFC
france24fr.description: Ciryl Gane a conservé son titre de champion incontesté des poids lourds de l'UFC après un combat très disputé face à l'Américain Josh Hokit au Madison Square Garden. Bousculé lors des premiers rounds, le Français a fait la différence en fin de combat pour s'imposer au terme de cinq reprises intenses. Une nouvelle victoire pour "Bon Gamin", figure de proue du MMA français, dans une discipline en plein essor en France. Récit de Shirli Sitbon et Ethan Hajji.

france24fr.title: L'Estonie accuse Moscou de tentative de sabotage et décide de fermer sa frontière
france24fr.description: ⁠L'Estonie fermera tous ⁠ses postes-frontières avec ​la Russie à compter du 1ᵉʳ décembre, a déclaré ​dimanche le ministre estonien des Affaires étrangères, à la suite d'une tentative d'incendie d'une entreprise du secteur de la défense ​imputée ‌par Tallinn à Moscou.

france24fr.title: Adama Barrow brigue un troisième mandat face à quatre adversaires en Gambie
france24fr.description: La Gambie se prépare à une nouvelle élection présidentielle avec cinq candidats en lice. Le président sortant Adama Barrow brigue un troisième mandat, face à quatre adversaires qui espèrent lui ravir le pouvoir. Un scrutin suivi de près dans un pays encore marqué par les années de régime de Yahya Jammeh. Récit d'Olivia Bizot.

france24fr.title: France - Turquie en direct : suivez le match décisif de la qualification pour les Bleus
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France affronte la Turquie ce dimanche à Bordeaux pour décrocher sa qualification en quarts de finale de Ligue des nations. Après leur défaite contre l'Italie jeudi à Milan, les Bleus n'ont plus le droit à l'erreur lors de cette ultime journée et pourront compter sur le retour de leur capitaine Kylian Mbappé pour cette rencontre décisive. Suivez le match en direct commenté sur France 24.

france24fr.title: Un commandant du Hamas tué par un drone israélien dans le sud de Gaza
france24fr.description: Un commandant de la branche militaire du mouvement islamiste palestinien Hamas a été tué par Israël dans le sud de la bande de Gaza, a fait savoir l'armée israélienne dimanche. Les bombardements se sont intensifiés ces derniers jours dans le sud du territoire palestinien.

france24fr.title: Au Niger, la détention de Moussa Kaka inquiète les défenseurs des droits humains
france24fr.description: Ancien correspondant de RFI au Niger, Moussa Kaka a été arrêté en août par les autorités militaires, qui n'ont officiellement annoncé sa détention qu'en octobre. Depuis plus de deux mois, plusieurs associations de défense des droits humains tentent d'alerter la communauté internationale sur sa situation, sans obtenir de réaction majeure à ce stade. Correspondance d'Harold Girard.

france24fr.title: MMA : Gane conserve sa ceinture au terme d'un rude combat face à Hokit
france24fr.description: Le combattant Ciryl Gane a conservé samedi son titre de champion incontesté des poids lourds de l'UFC au terme d'un combat très éprouvant contre l'Américain Josh Hokit. Premier Français au sommet de la catégorie reine du MMA, Ciryl Gane, alias "Bon Gamin", défendait pour la première fois à New York son titre face à "The Incredible Hok", nouvelle attraction chez les poids lourds. Il a été donné vainqueur au cours de cinq rounds très intenses face à un challenger très agressif.

france24fr.title: Le travail du photoreporter Antoni Lallican en Ukraine raconté dans un livre hommage
france24fr.description: Tué le 3 octobre 2025 alors qu'il travaillait en Ukraine, le photojournaliste français Antoni Lallican laisse derrière lui un important travail consacré au Donbass. L'ouvrage "Le soleil de l'Ukraine se lève dans le Donbass", publié en français, en anglais et en ukrainien, rassemble une partie de ses photographies. Aïda Belloulid, sa compagne, revient sur ce livre, sur son travail de reporter et sur l'enquête ouverte après sa mort, attribuée à une attaque de drone.

france24fr.title: Méta, Google, Microsoft ... L'Europe sous perfusion technologique ?
france24fr.description: La panne mondiale de l'écosystème de Microsoft relance les interrogations sur la dépendance technologique de l'Europe. Notre invité Guillaume Limare, auteur de "Vivre sans Google", analyse cet incident et ce qu'il révèle de la place prise par les géants américains du numérique dans les infrastructures européennes.

france24fr.title: Une frappe israélienne dans le sud de Gaza vise un responsable du Hamas
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne affirme avoir ciblé dimanche un responsable de la branche militaire du Hamas dans le sud de la bande de Gaza. Des sources palestiniennes évoquent de leur côté la mort d'un commandant du mouvement. Une nouvelle frappe alors que la situation sur place continue de se dégrader. Les précisions de Rami Abou Jamus, journaliste indépendant à Gaza pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Explosions à Bahreïn, l'Iran revendique une attaque contre une base américaine
france24fr.description: L'Iran revendique une attaque de drones contre un site militaire américain à Bahreïn. L'opération aurait eu lieu tôt dans la matinée, entre 4 h 30 et 6 h, alors que les tensions dans la région semblaient s'apaiser. Les habitants ont rapidement été invités à se mettre à l'abri. Les précisions de Léa Delfolie, correspondante à Dubaï.

zeit.title: Südamerika-Reise: Papst warnt vor Zerstörung des Amazonas-Regenwalds
»Tatort« Münster: Das macht doch überhaupt keinen Sinn
zeit.description: Im neuen Münsteraner »Tatort« geht ein Gardetanz-Trainer an vergifteten Kamellen zugrunde. Dabei verheddert sich die Folge in ihrem Kostüm.

zeit.title: Gaza: Vier Staaten fordern Israel zum Stopp der Blockade von Gaza-Hilfe auf
zeit.description: Israel solle Durchlass für humanitäre Hilfe nach Gaza geben, verlangen vier Staaten. Im Westjordanland hat Israels Armee einen AFP-Journalisten festgenommen. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Eishockey: Eishockey-U20-WM ohne Russland - Russen kündigen Protest an
Deutsche Eishockey Liga: Eisbären Berlin verlieren auch gegen Schwenningen
Jürgen Klopp: Klopp spricht sich für neue Fifa-Führung aus
zeit.description: Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp hat den Fifa-Präsidenten Gianni Infantino deutlich kritisiert. Als Gegenkandidaten schlägt er Fifa-Direktor Arsène Wenger vor.

zeit.title: Proteste in Tschechien: Sie rufen: »Nie wieder 4:36 Uhr!«
zeit.description: Hunderttausende Tschechen demonstrieren gegen ihre Regierung. Es geht um Angriffe auf die Medien, linientreue Kultur – und klandestine nächtliche Parlamentssitzungen.

zeit.title: Wirtschaftspolitik: US-Finanzminister fordert neuen Nvidia-Chef von außerhalb
Notfälle: Wegen Pizzaofen: Zwei Männer mit Kohlenmonoxid vergiftet
Fußball-Nationalmannschaft: Klopp: Holland-Kapitän van Dijk ist schön und kann singen
Nvidia-Skandal: Mutmaßliche Spionin Alice Huang soll nicht mehr bei Megaspeed arbeiten
zeit.description: Die Affäre des Ex-Nvidia-Chefs soll am Umgehen von Exportverboten durch die Firma Megaspeed beteiligt gewesen sein. Nach Firmenangaben spielt sie dort »keine Rolle« mehr.

zeit.title: Fußball: Ronaldinho feiert Comeback als Profifußballer in Italien
zeit.description: Erstmals seit 2015 ist Ronaldinho wieder bei einem Pflichtspiel aufgelaufen. Der italienische Drittligist Ravenna FC erweiterte dafür die Tribüne seines Stadions.

zeit.title: Pierre-Louis Vuitton: Geschichte im Gepäck
zeit.description: Seit dem 19. Jahrhundert prägen die Koffer von Louis Vuitton das moderne Reisen. Pierre-Louis Vuitton, sein Urururenkel, baut sie noch immer.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Streit um Russlands WM-Teilnahme: Russland kann nicht an der Junioren-Weltmeisterschaft in Kanada teilnehmen
nzz.description: Der Internationale Sportgerichtshof hat den Ausschluss Russlands von Eishockey-Weltmeisterschaften aufgehoben. Doch zahlreiche Länder wehren sich gegen die Rückkehr der Russen. Was bedeutet das für das kommende Turnier? Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Ein Router in Arkansas, ein zweiter in Texas: Viele Fragen zum landesweiten Flugstopp bleiben offen
nzz.description: Laut der amerikanischen Luftfahrtbehörde waren Erneuerungsarbeiten am Kommunikationsnetz der Flugsicherung für das Grounding am Freitag verantwortlich.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Huthi-Miliz zielt erneut auf Saudiarabien +++ Iran greift Bahrain mit Drohnen an
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Estland schliesst Grenzen zu Russland wegen eines Anschlags auf eine Drohnenfabrik
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Migrationskrise in Europa: 1500 Menschen erreichen die Kanaren an einem einzigen Tag
nzz.description: Über die griechischen Inseln, die Balkanroute oder den Ärmelkanal versuchen täglich Migranten, unter Lebensgefahr nach Europa zu gelangen. Die Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Korruptionsverdacht gegen Ex-Minister: Die im Wald vergrabenen Millionen stürzen Orbans Partei weiter in die Krise
nzz.description: Peter Magyars Amt für Vermögensrückgewinnung entdeckt bündelweise Geld im Gesamtwert von 16 Millionen Franken. Der Regierungschef sieht darin einen Beweis für die Korruption im System Orban.

nzz.title: VIDEO - SpaceX fängt die obere Stufe der Starship-Rakete erstmals auf
nzz.description: Rund 20 Stunden nach dem Start kehrte das Starship zum Weltraumbahnhof Starbase im US-Bundesstaat Texas zurück und wurde dort von Greifarmen am Startturm aufgefangen. Wie das funktionierte und was dafür alles nötig war lesen Sie hier.

nzz.title: Ein Mann der Mitte? Die AfD nominiert den Fussballweltmeister Thomas Berthold für das Amt des deutschen Bundespräsidenten
nzz.description: Berthold fiel nicht nur einmal mit einem Hang zu Verschwörungserzählungen auf. Seine Nominierung illustriert, was die AfD unter dem Begriff der Mitte versteht.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN KULTUR - Sarah Elena Müller gewinnt mit «Unwucht» den Schweizer Buchpreis 2026
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.title: Weltcup-Slalom in Levi: Loïc Meillard fährt auf den dritten Platz – Lucas Pinheiro Braathen sichert sich den Sieg
nzz.description: Wie bereits im Vorjahr landet der Neuenburger in Finnland auf dem Podest.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Carmelle gewinnt für die Philippinen die erste Ausgabe des Eurovision Song Contest Asia
nzz.description: Beim ersten Eurovision Song Contest Asia traten elf Länder gegeneinander an. Bangkok wurde zur Bühne für ein neues Kapitel des Musikwettbewerbs.

nzz.title: Leonardo Genoni führt den EV Zug in seinem 1000. Einsatz zum Sieg – doch der Frieden im Klub bleibt brüchig
nzz.description: Der EV Zug fügt den ZSC Lions erst die zweite Saisonniederlage zu. Die aggressive Transferstrategie verschafft Goodwill. Der übertüncht die vielschichtigen Probleme des Klubs.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Machtkampf in der Fifa: Arsène Wenger wird laut «L'Équipe» nicht für das Präsidentenamt kandidieren
nzz.description: Seit der WM im Sommer 2026 ist der Kampf um das Fifa-Präsidium entbrannt. Im März findet die Wahl des Präsidenten statt. Die jüngsten Entwicklungen und die Hintergründe im Überblick.

nzz.title: Mann stürzt in Österreich wegen Lawine in eine tiefe Kluft und stirbt
nzz.description: Das Unglück geschah am Stubaier Gletscher. Der Mann konnte zwar geborgen werden, doch sein Leben war nicht mehr zu retten.

nzz.title: Die USA verlieren laut Medienberichten den Status «masernfrei»
nzz.description: Das Masernvirus sei das ansteckendste Virus der Welt, sagt der Chef der Weltgesundheitsorganisation.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Lage im Gazastreifen: Israel tötet hochrangigen Hamas-Kommandanten
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist instabil, die humanitäre Not im Gazastreifen ist gross. Der Friedensplan der USA wurde bisher nur teilweise umgesetzt. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

observador.title: As notícias das 21h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Trump recebeu Bolsonaro nos EUA após eleições brasileiras?
observador.description: Fotografia publicada nas redes sociais mostra Trump a receber senador nos EUA após as eleições brasileiras. Imagem foi gerada por inteligência artificial e não corresponde a um encontro real.

observador.title: Trump pediu investigação a eleições no Brasil?
observador.description: Publicações nas redes sociais e em portais brasileiros sugerem que Trump quer investigação a eleições que disse "parecerem viciadas". Mas o apelo não veio do Presidente dos EUA.

observador.title: Imagem mostra recolha de iPhones após ataque em Ormuz?
observador.description: Um navio afundou em outubro, no Estreito de Ormuz, e desde então que nas redes sociais circulam dezenas de imagens que mostram Iphones à deriva no mar. Serão verdadeiras?

observador.title: Arranca contagem para escolha de PR de Cabo Verde
observador.description: A votação decorreu de forma pacífica nas cerca de mil mesas nas ilhas e 240 no estrangeiro, tendo o dia ficado marcado por apelos dos principais intervenientes políticos à participação.

observador.title: Presidente do CDS-PP lembra que "PS é casa de socialistas"
observador.description: Melo lançou mensagem "muito clara" a ex-militantes: "Quem deixa o CDS e se junta ao PS, nem é democrata-cristão, nem tem nada a ver com o CDS, passa a socialista."

observador.title: 20h. Rússia adverte para regresso de ensaios nucleares
observador.description: Representante permanente da Rússia junto da Agência Internacional da Energia Atómica fala em resposta adequada, se tal acontecer. Ainda, Estónia fecha fronteiras com a Rússia a partir do próximo mês.

observador.title: Segredos do carro voador que a Xpeng mostrou na Web Summit
observador.description: A Xpeng, um dos construtores chineses mais tecnológicos, surpreendeu a Web Summit ao apresentar o Aridge, um carro voador que propõe uma solução para circular simultaneamente pela estrada e pelo ar.

observador.title: Governo angolano pede firmeza da polícia para reduzir mortes
observador.description: Angola assinalou o Dia Mundial em Memória das Vítimas da Estrada com um apelo à "atuação firme, legal e consequente" contra comportamentos de risco.

observador.title: Raimundo critica "obsessão ideológica" com privatizações
observador.description: Para Paulo Raimundo as responsabilidades pela situação dos Açores não podem ser atribuídas exclusivamente ao Governo da República.

observador.title: Judoca Rochele Nunes conquista bronze em Zagreb
observador.description: Rochele Nunes, que foi mãe em maio de 2025, volta três anos depois a subir ao pódio de uma competição de categoria superior, com o Grand Prix a estar acima do Open Europeu.

observador.title: Ventura viabilizará propostas "cabíveis" para reduzir custos
observador.description: Dentro das "propostas que são orçamentalmente cabíveis", o presidente do Chega adiantou que vai viabilizar todas aquelas que "implicarem menos custos".

observador.title: Os bons e os maus
observador.description: Considerarmos alguém má pessoa não tem de ser uma atribuição impulsiva, gratuita ou volátil. É uma forma de colocarmos a sufrágio a bondade de que somos capazes.

observador.title: 19h. Estónia vai fechar fronteiras com Rússia no próximo mês
observador.description: Ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros da Estónia diz que decisão se deve a ataque de sabotagem da Rússia à indústria de defesa do país. Ainda, preço dos combustíveis volta a descer amanhã.

observador.title: Tenho PHDA ou só estou distraído? Como manter o foco
observador.description: Sete tabs abertas, duas televisões e um telemóvel: a sua atenção aguenta? Distrai-se com tudo ou será PHDA? Onde foi parar o nosso foco? E há truques para treinar a atenção?

observador.title: Montefiore: "O regime do Irão vai desintegrar-se por dentro"
observador.description: Não é possível compreender o Médio Oriente sem compreender o fim do Império Otomano e não haverá paz enquanto se pensar que o vizinho nos vai atacar. Conversa com o historiador Simon Segab Montefiore.

observador.title: Mais do que feitiços, o Bruxo não perdeu o seu encanto
observador.description: Ronaldinho Gaúcho, um dos oito magníficos com Mundial de Clubes, Champions e Bola de Ouro, voltou aos relvados pelo Ravenna, na Serie C italiana. Os 46 anos já pesam mas tudo valeu a pena – e ganhou.

observador.title: Foi provado que nanotecnologia de vacinas afeta esperma?
observador.description: Publicados nas redes sociais, estudo de universidade israelita e vídeo provariam que componentes das vacinas que usam tecnologia mRNA ficam no esperma durante 168 dias. Será verdade?

spiegel.title: Mario Basler: Ex-Fußballnationalspieler rettet Unfallopfer aus Auto
spiegel.description: Ex-Fußballnationalspieler Mario Basler ist nach einem Autounfall zum Ersthelfer geworden: Den Fahrer des verunglückten Autos zog er laut eigener Aussage aus dem noch qualmenden Wagen. Für Basler eine »selbstverständliche« Sache.

spiegel.title: Lesen: Warum Jugendliche Bücher meiden und ihr Denken leidet
spiegel.description: Vor allem in Deutschland sinkt die Lesekompetenz drastisch, zeigen Studien. Der Sprachpsychologe Falk Huettig erklärt, warum Jugendliche Bücher meiden und das sogar ihr Denkvermögen gefährden kann.

spiegel.title: The Oak Ridge Boys: Country-Sänger Richard Sterban mit 83 Jahren gestorben
spiegel.description: »Um-poppa-um-poppa, mow, mow«: Mit seinem lautmalerischen Bassgesang prägte Richard Sterban die Songs des Country-Ensembles The Oak Ridge Boys. Auch mit Elvis war er aufgetreten. Nun ist er mit 83 Jahren gestorben.

spiegel.title: Tschechien: Massenproteste gegen Rundfunkreform
spiegel.description: Die tschechische Regierung will den öffentlich-rechtlichen Rundfunk künftig aus Staatsmitteln statt durch Rundfunkgebühren finanzieren. In Prag kam es nun zu Massenprotesten gegen die Pläne.

spiegel.title: Deutschland: Wie ich zwischen Kirche und Sozialismus aufwuchs - Kolumne
spiegel.description: Als Kind konnte ich mich nur schwer zwischen Kirche und Sozialismus entscheiden, wie es von mir ständig gefordert wurde. Daran hat sich bis heute nicht viel geändert.

spiegel.title: The Goodforces: Diese Agentur will Rot-Rot-Grün an die Macht bringen
spiegel.description: Bis 2029 will The Goodforces eine Mehrheit für SPD, Grüne und Linke mobilisieren. Noch sprechen die Umfragen dagegen. Die Berliner Agentur aber prägt längst etliche Debatten.

spiegel.title: Fifa: Jürgen Klopp wünscht sich Abgang von Gianni Infantino
spiegel.description: Die Europäer wollen den hochumstrittenen Fifa-Chef Gianni Infantino stürzen. Nun meldet sich auch Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp zu Wort – mit einer deutlichen Ansage.

spiegel.title: Spanien vor der Wahl: Verliert Linken-Posterboy Pedro Sánchez sein Land an die Rechten?
spiegel.description: Weil er sich gegen Trumps Irankrieg stellte, wurde Pedro Sánchez weltweit zum Held der Linken. Doch nun droht ausgerechnet dem gefeierten Spanier ein schneller Absturz – mit schwerwiegenden Folgen.

spiegel.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown beim NFL-Spiel in München: Deutschland hat ein neues Football-Idol
spiegel.description: Beim NFL-Spiel in München war der beste deutsche Footballspieler der Geschichte dabei: Amon-Ra St. Brown. Der Offensivstar zeigte seine Weltklasse – und welche Bedeutung er für deutsche Footballfans hat.

spiegel.title: Estland: Regierung will Grenzen zu Russland zum 1. Dezember schließen
spiegel.description: Der russische Militärgeheimdienst soll hinter einem versuchten Brandanschlag auf einen Drohnenhersteller in Estland stecken. Darum will die Regierung in Tallinn zum 1. Dezember alle Grenzen zum Nachbarland schließen lassen.

spiegel.title: X von Elon Musk: Die Zone, die Donald Trumps Jünger mit Shit fluteten, war ihr eigener Garten
spiegel.description: Als Tesla-Chef Elon Musk Twitter kaufte und zu einem Naherholungsgebiet für Nationalisten umbaute, jubelte das Trump-Lager. Dann wiederholten die Rechten den Fehler der Linken: Sie vergaßen die echte Welt.

phys-org.title: The experiments improving our understanding of volcanic tsunamis
phys-org.description: Tsunamis triggered by volcanic eruptions are poorly understood because of the complex dynamics governing how falling rocks and ash interact with seawater to generate waves. As a result, it is difficult to anticipate whether a volcanic flow will trigger a tsunami and, if so, how big it will be. Researchers have used laboratory experiments to study this process, but little is known about how well these models mimic reality.

phys-org.title: Tangled quantum whirlpools caught unraveling in an ultracold gas
phys-org.description: When a cloud of atoms is cooled close to absolute zero, its atoms can merge into a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC): an exotic fluid in which atoms across the whole cloud share a single quantum state. Current theories predict that as a disordered quantum gas settles into this ordered state, a tangle of tiny vortices should form and gradually unravel.

phys-org.title: Climate response: Why previous warming makes all the difference
phys-org.description: Global temperatures may continue to rise even after human CO₂ emissions stop. The temperature change that follows is known as the zero emissions commitment (ZEC), and it is often assumed to be close to zero. A study led by the Met Office Hadley Center, with co-authors from several institutions including the University of Liverpool, found that the temperature response depends on how much warming has already occurred.

phys-org.title: Giant, prehistoric rodent fossils discovered in southern Thailand
phys-org.description: An international team of paleontologists, including researchers from McGill University, has discovered "remarkably large" rodent fossils in the pit of a mine in southern Thailand. phys-org.title: New observations challenge evidence for an 'outsize' black hole in the early universe
phys-org.description: A recent reanalysis of the outsize black hole galaxy UHZ1 using existing X-ray data and new infrared observations challenges a previous groundbreaking claim. Three years ago, this galaxy made news for hosting an unusually massive and heavily dust-obscured black hole formed through direct collapse. Led by Fan Zou of the University of Michigan, the new study reports no signs of hidden black hole activity. The paper, published in The Astrophysical Journal on Oct. 14, suggests UHZ1 could be a low-ma

phys-org.description: For a decade, the 1.5C goal has served as the north star of climate action, a line nations pledged to hold to avoid the worst ravages of a warming planet.

phys-org.title: Is this iconic black hole image accurate? New study delivers an independent result
phys-org.description: On April 10, 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) Collaboration revealed the first picture of a black hole. The object is at the center of a galaxy known as M87, about 55 million light-years away.

phys-org.title: Urban expansion causes ecological collapse in streams in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area
phys-org.description: The advance of urbanization in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area in Brazil is causing the collapse of food webs in local streams. A study published in August in the journal Nature Cities reveals that the impact of the metropolis goes far beyond a simple reduction in species. Degradation selectively eliminates organisms based on their size and simplifies ecological interactions. Networks of 190 connections plummet to just three.

phys-org.title: A dead star is flashing radio waves every 8 minutes, and its partner looks a lot like the sun
phys-org.description: Since 2022, astronomers have been puzzling over a new kind of cosmic object called long-period radio transients. These are objects that emit bright flashes of radio waves into space every few minutes to every few hours. Some have been traced back to binary systems consisting of a small, dim, cool star called a red dwarf in orbit with a stellar remnant called a white dwarf.

phys-org.title: A cosmic magnifying glass could reveal the same supernova two more times in roughly 70 years
phys-org.description: Thanks to the gravitational lensing caused by a massive galaxy cluster and high-resolution images from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers discovered an exploding star when the universe was 4.9 billion years old. The discovery paper, posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 23, presents a prediction for when the rest of the distorted images of SN Ares will arrive.

phys-org.title: Some of the oldest rocks ever discovered shed light on Earth's early history
phys-org.description: Earth is approximately 4.5 billion years old, according to estimates. However, rocks dating back to the planet's earliest days are extremely rare. Hence the excitement over the discovery in northern China of some of the oldest known rocks on Earth, dating back 3.95 billion years. And one of the reasons for all the attention is that they're revealing new clues about how Earth's crust formed and evolved.

phys-org.title: World's largest freshwater lake is recovering after decades of decline
phys-org.description: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds around 20% of the world's surface freshwater, making it the most voluminous freshwater lake (Lake Superior on the United States–Canada border is the largest by surface area). This makes the lake one of the most important environments for biodiversity—in fact, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1996 because of this. Yet it has shown considerable decline over the last century, with aridification spreading across East Asia.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: The Rare-Earth Game
proj-syn.description: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive. And the West will probably not achieve self-sufficiency in this critical sector, but it will keep seeking to reduce its vulnerability to a supply shock through expensive capacity duplication and stockpiles.

proj-syn.title: Why Research Matters
proj-syn.description: Over the past 21 months, in the country that has leveraged research to greatest effect, the government is slashing funding for it, closing centers where it is done, politicizing grant-making decisions, and bullying its single biggest engine: universities. The costs will be far greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Africa Needs a Different Kind of Climate Finance
proj-syn.description: Roughly half of the climate finance that flows to Africa comes in the form of debt, with multilateral and bilateral development-finance institutions often lending at commercial rates to economies already struggling to carry the added costs. To maximize fiscal space, the instruments used to deliver climate finance need to change.

proj-syn.title: Effective Climate Action Requires Capable States
proj-syn.description: With delegations from around the world gathering for another international climate conference, the question today is not whether governments should do more to address the climate crisis, but whether they even have the capabilities to do so. After 40 years of free-market orthodoxy, many simply do not.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Mexico Defying Latin America’s Right Turn?
proj-syn.description: How Mexico’s left has managed to retain strong support is a key question of contemporary Latin American politics. The most likely answer centers on the ruling Morena party’s pragmatic brand of left-wing politics, which combines bold redistributive policies, greater security, and a willingness to compromise in the name of both.

proj-syn.title: The Digital-Currency Divide
proj-syn.description: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. But while the Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their plans, the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro.

proj-syn.title: The ASEAN Paradox
proj-syn.description: As the Association of Southeast Asian Nations gathers for its 49th Summit, several rifts have exposed the group’s institutional shortcomings. But amid a fracturing global order, ASEAN must choose: turn its convening authority into concerted action or be reduced to an arena for great-power rivalry.

proj-syn.title: Medical AI Needs Bedside Manners
proj-syn.description: Even the most accurate medical AI tools have little value if they make patients uneasy or doctors find them too cumbersome. A comfort-by-design approach could overcome these obstacles by involving patients and practitioners in development and ensuring that new systems work with existing medical practices.

proj-syn.title: Reviving the Legacy of Reykjavík
proj-syn.description: As nuclear threats grow, AI accelerates, and international law comes under strain, the world urgently needs a renewed commitment to dialogue. Today's leaders can find a template in the landmark 1986 summit between then US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dreams Exceed Its Grid
proj-syn.description: Europe is racing to expand its AI data-center capacity, but its power grids are already strained, and local communities are increasingly pushing back against new construction. Achieving technological sovereignty will require less grandstanding and more practical solutions that make better use of existing resources.

proj-syn.title: What the US Midterms Could Mean for AI
proj-syn.description: Now that the Democrats will hold sizable majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, they have an opening to push for long-overdue legislation to steer AI development toward the common good. Private companies should not have the power to decide unilaterally which risks the public will bear.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Publish AI-Generated Articles!
proj-syn.description: Peer-reviewed academic journals exist to advance our knowledge and understanding by publishing the best work being done in a given field. If that is the goal, and the best reviewers—both human and AI—agree that an article generated by AI meets that standard, why should a journal's editors reject it?

proj-syn.title: The AI Industry Should Make Something People Want
proj-syn.description: AI companies have alienated Americans by forcing them to bear the costs of their products while treating their consent as optional. With voters across the United States rejecting data centers, the incoming Congress has an opportunity to enact meaningful regulation and hold the industry accountable.

proj-syn.title: It’s the Corruption, Stupid
proj-syn.description: Fed up with Donald Trump and his family's blatant profiteering, Americans dealt Republicans a resounding defeat in this month’s midterm elections. Democrats won by linking corruption to the cost-of-living crisis, but the party’s establishment remains compromised and must clean house before 2028.

proj-syn.title: The Fed's Risky Retreat From Transparency
proj-syn.description: Kevin Warsh, the new chair of the US Federal Reserve, is not wrong to abandon the practice of forward guidance. But if he continues to withhold information about how the central bank intends to assess the economic outlook and determine the appropriate stance of monetary policy, he is in for a rude awakening.

proj-syn.title: An Owl’s Guide to US-China Coexistence
proj-syn.description: In 2027 and beyond, the United States should lay the foundation for a stable coexistence with China, not a contest to “win.” A clear-eyed approach is needed to help make “the world safe for diversity,” as John F. Kennedy put it in 1963.

proj-syn.title: AI Investors Have Overlooked Obvious Risks
proj-syn.description: Prior to the US midterm elections on November 3, financial markets had been treating generative AI as some kind of unstoppable force that could not be hampered by higher interest rates or political and social resistance. But now reality may be setting in.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Over the past few decades, we have adopted a new framework for thinking about privacy that centers our experience in the digital realm, conflates privacy with secrecy, and fails to account for the insecurity surveillance generates. As a result, even privacy advocates often undermine their own cause.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Nvidia’s Startup Funding Deals Hit A Record. What’s Next After Huang?
crunchbase.description: Before it was thrust into crisis this week, Nvidia was steadily continuing its pace as one of the busiest startup investors around, including backing many of the biggest venture deals of 2026. We take a fresh look at where Nvidia and its venture arm NVentures have been investing and what the future could hold.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Agentic AI And Infrastructure Are Still On A Roll
crunchbase.description: It was another big week for AI-related startup financings. Mirendil, a developer of agentic AI for R&D, led the pack with a $1 billion series A, followed by Mercor, which secured $750 million to connect AI developers with human experts.

crunchbase.title: Protein Startups Are Selling Lots Of Snacks And Drinks. Our Sample Tasting Found Most Neither Great Nor Horrible
crunchbase.description: As we chronicled earlier this week, both startups and established food brands are making it simpler than ever to up protein intake. From sodas to snack bars to ice cream, it’s now possible to get a fix of this coveted macronutrient with foods and drinks more commonly associated with sugar, starch and fat. But, do they taste good? To find out, we hit up a local Target for a selection of protein foods sold by venture-backed startups and subjected them to a taste test. Here are our findings.

crunchbase.title: How Founders Can Reduce Platform Risk Before It Threatens Growth
crunchbase.description: Founders should treat dependence on app stores as infrastructure risk, since a sudden removal can disrupt customer access, subscriptions and revenue with no reliable path to reinstatement. Sharing his experience, Yakov Filippenko, founder and CEO of Intch, suggests that building and testing alternative access and payment channels before a crisis can help keep the business operating.

crunchbase.title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
crunchbase.description: Recent startup investment has shifted away from meat substitutes and toward stuffing more protein into other packaged foods and drinks. It’s a fad that’s obvious on supermarket shelves, where startups and established brands alike relentlessly tout the added protein in their noodles, pancakes, cereals, energy bars, popcorn and so on. We take a look.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Nubank Alum Raises $14M For Colombia’s Palomma To Tackle Rent Payments, Landlord Financing
crunchbase.description: Colombia-based startup, Palomma, has raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Mexican venture firm Cometa to expand its financial services business for landlords, tenants and property managers, Crunchbase News has exclusively learned.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Seeks Record $88.5B Tied To Public Market Debut
crunchbase.description: Anthropic is seeking to secure up to $88.5 billion in its planned IPO and a concurrent private placement, potentially making it the largest-ever fundraise tied to a public market debut. On Tuesday, the AI giant submitted an updated S-1 filing for its upcoming public offering, unveiling new details including a proposed share price range offering size.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Unicorn Board Tops 1,900 Companies In October, With 34 Companies Joining — Half Under 4 Years Old
crunchbase.description: A total of 34 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in October, adding more than $96 billion in value and $14.8 billion in total funding to the board. The board also reached a new record of 1,900 private companies last month, along with a new record for the U.S. with more than 1,000 private unicorn companies.

crunchbase.title: Startup Founders Are Using AI To File Patents. Here’s Where DIY Becomes A Liability.
crunchbase.description: AI can help startups reduce patent preparation costs, but DIY applications may overlook critical issues. In this guest commentary, attorneys Michael Drapkin and Nathan Mutter of AI-Native law firm Landfall IP, argue that combining AI with legal expertise can produce more efficient, commercially valuable patent protection that withstands investor scrutiny and is harder for competitors to circumvent.

crunchbase.title: Series A In 2026: Capital Is Flowing Faster, But Fewer Startups Are Making The Cut
crunchbase.description: More money is pouring into Series A rounds, but it isn’t opening the door to more startups. U.S. companies have raised $42 billion at that stage this year through October, up roughly 60% year over year, while deal counts remain on pace with the past few years, Crunchbase data shows.
